paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. The LORD has a Servant, and He is nothing like the loud, shiny gods people trust. The LORD says, "I will put My Spirit on Him, and He will bring justice to the nations" (Isaiah 42:1). He doesn't win by shouting in the streets, and He doesn't give up halfway, because the LORD says He "will not grow weak or discouraged before He has established justice on the earth" (Isaiah 42:2, 4). Matthew says these words are fulfilled in Jesus (Matthew 12:17-21).

Now look at how gentle He is. "A bruised reed He will not break and a smoldering wick He will not extinguish" (Isaiah 42:3). Baker, I know what it feels like to be a worn-out, barely flickering thing in the back of a drawer. This is good news for anybody who feels that way, because the Servant doesn't snuff out the weak. He is strong AND kind, and that's a rare combo, even in my bakery.

And the One behind all of it is worth trusting. He made the heavens, He gives breath to people, and He says, "I am the LORD; that is My name!" (Isaiah 42:5, 8). He calls His Servant "a light to the nations," to "open the eyes of the blind" and bring out those "sitting in darkness" (Isaiah 42:6-7). So when life gets dark, you can hold on to this: the God who spoke the plan ahead of time is faithful to finish it (Isaiah 42:9).
